 | D26 | **A lane PR is recognised by its head branch stem or its title prefix, both as GitHub reports them when the run starts.** CTRL-lane-gate (#1300) keys the codex lane on `pkg/codex-` (LANES.md, AGENTS.md step 4) or a `CX-` title. All teams push as Mark's GitHub login, so the author cannot tell lanes apart; a Codex PR pushed from another stem with a non-`CX-` title escapes the gate, and a title edit re-runs the gate (`edited` is one of its triggers). The gate is its own workflow on `pull_request_target`, so GitHub runs the base commit's workflow file and `risk_tier.py`, checked out from the base only; the PR head is fetched as git objects for the diff and never checked out or run, so a PR cannot delete, skip or loosen the gate. A base without the gate's flags fails closed. The gate blocks a merge only once main requires the `lane-gate` check (a ruleset change after this PR merges). | CTRL-lane-gate | If a Codex PR is ever seen on another stem, key the gate on something GitHub ties to the pusher (a separate bot account or deploy key for the lane) instead of names. |
 | D27 | **During the G1 freeze, a PR's paths are a good enough proxy for whether its work serves G1, and a PR's opening time identifies the work already in flight.** `tools/g1_scope.txt` lists the paths G1 needs: every broker package the G1 binaries import (the image's six binaries, the guest bridge, the seller tool, the checker, clock-boot and hostdisk), minus the learning packages Mark's Tight choice freezes, plus the image, the openclaw and Codex guests, CTRL-spike and the project machinery. G1 names one model route (D-104; Mark 2026-10-14 19:35Z, "ChatGPT plan" on Decisions card cmsg_01R63S2yrPkq32thy8WQCuvDFt5XhL8peUFCaddWFQZ4YR): the owner's ChatGPT plan through the broker-held Codex provider worker. That route is not wired today, so wiring it is G1 work: the plan-login chain #807, #1015, #1014, #1314 and #1264, enabled by #809. So guest/codex/ and broker/provagent/ (which #1314 creates; the existence test exempts it until then) are listed, and the API-key adapters' own files (broker/route/openai*, broker/route/anthropic*) are off the list. broker/route/ is listed file by file, so a new file there needs a list amendment; the code the adapters share with the guest's chat path stays listed and only the frozen rows' labels hold their halves of it. A row whose work is not G1 but edits only G1 packages (plan routes, guest sovereignty, recall) still passes: only row labels hold those. Every PR opened before the list's `since` time passes, whatever its row's state (building, review, in review, escalated), so work in flight when the freeze merged finishes (Mark 2026-10-14: "don't freeze PRs mid flight", "let current PRs finish"). The opening time is the pull_request event's `created_at`, which the author cannot set, so the exemption needs no snapshot and cannot be spoofed by a branch or title. The exemption is keyed on `created_at`, so a dormant, reopened or retargeted PR keeps it (tracked in #1717). A later PR for work already under way (a split, or a rebuild after escalation) gets an `exempt-pr N` amend; the failure message says so. The push that merges #1687 sets `since` to its own time, so a PR opened while that push's CI runs is the one gap, routed the same way. "Passes in QEMU" means the e2e DONE line reads fail=0 xfail=0 blocked=0: a run with guest-task XFAIL (#1701) or phone control not driven does not lift the freeze. The workflow runs the base commit's copy on `pull_request_target`, so a PR cannot widen the list, flip `freeze off`, move `since` or exempt itself; it blocks a merge only once main requires the `g1-freeze` check. A plain Re-run replays the old event and its old base, so after an amend merges the owner pushes or edits the PR to re-run. | G1-freeze-a–f | If G1 work lands outside the list, amend the list in its own PR (the base copy decides). When a G1-e2e (#1688) QEMU run's DONE line reads fail=0 xfail=0 blocked=0, a PR sets `freeze off` citing that run's URL and its log: the `image` workflow, job `build (a)`, step "Boot test (Secure Boot on) and end-to-end run", which must show `ci_boot: G1 PROVEN` (image/ci_boot.sh prints it to that step's log, with a prefix only the host uses, and only then and only in a run that passed every check, so a red run prints `ci_boot: G1 NOT PROVEN (run failed)`; the run fails if the guest console carries the text, and the console artifact never holds it). The counts behind it come from the in-guest driver's DONE line, which the host cross-checks: exactly one strictly anchored DONE, last, equal to the PASS/FAIL/XFAIL/XPASS/BLOCKED step lines, with every echoed guest line (the boot echo and the e2e driver lines) sanitised and prefixed `console| `, and driver lines accepted only under the `box-e2e[pid]:` tag. A guest that forged the whole console would still pass that, so it raises the cost and keeps the verdict host-only; it is not attestation; the workflow and files can be removed later. If a PR's opening time proves a poor proxy for in-flight work, add `exempt-pr` lines. |
 | D28 | **Arming at the last accept is safe if the head is the accepted head, and records need no PR push.** RECORDS-INLINE (#1816) and ARM-AT-ACCEPT (#1819), both part of #1691, approved by Mark 2026-10-15 (cmsg_01R63S2yrPkq32thy8WQCuvDCVDGCf9kEBbZRpfxDeybYm; D-120). Records stay bot-only: `.github/workflows/records.yml` runs daily, so `tools/premerge.py` has no exemption and a feature PR carries no record commit. The arm call takes no expected head and all teams push as one login, so a push does not disarm; the arming session re-reads the head after arming and disarms on a change, and sessions disable auto-merge before pushing and re-review a new head. `premerge.py --needs-mark` lists PRs touching the permission/review paths, which Mark merges. | PLAN.md tooling, not SPEC.md; docs/OPERATING.md §4, §7 | If a push to an armed PR ever merges unreviewed, make premerge a required check. If parallel merges are rolled back, restore the merge worker. |
+| D29 | **Markdown whose only readers are checks the records run executes can ride the records run, and the Go build cache is safe because only main writes what PRs restore.** CI-PATHS (#1817) widens D23's set with README.md, PLAN.md, SPEC.md, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, docs/OPERATING.md, docs/LANES.md, the two *-HISTORY files, two orphan notes, and `*.md` under docs/development, docs/learning and docs/security. The records run now also runs tests.test_product_name, test_specslice and test_g1_scope, so doclint, board, trace, metrics, risk_tier, specslice, g1_scope and the product-name check still read every one of them. Every non-Markdown file and every Markdown a Go test or go:embed reads (docs/owners-guide.md, by a broker Go test) stays full. Checked by grepping the repo's Go, Python, shell and workflow sources for each file name on 2026-10-15; the self-check in tests/test_ci_scope.py walks `git ls-files` and refuses an executable record. tools/g1_scope.py reuses `is_record`, so widening the set widens the freeze's records-only pass; harmless while tools/g1_scope.txt allows every added path. The broker and machines jobs restore `go-build` caches keyed on go.mod/go.sum (vendored, so no module cache) on every event and save them only on a push to main, with `$GOCACHE/fuzz` removed first. Go trusts stored outputs rather than re-hashing them, so the defence is GitHub's ref scoping: only runs of main's code on main write the scope that PRs restore, and a test refuses `actions/cache` in any `pull_request_target` or `workflow_run` workflow. |
